sentences.text: Shri S.S.Rajput - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Naresh Singh Tomar - Advocate for respondent No
 Order

This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/claimant valuing it Rs.2,00,000/-
against the award dated 02.05.2009 passed by Additional MACT, Vidisha, in Claim Case No.28/2008 whereby learned MACT has dismissed the claim of the appellant.

2. The necessary facts for disposal of this appeal are that on 16.09.2007 the appellant after labour work was going on Shamshabad road, at that juncture, near Sultaniya driver of tractor bearing registration No.MP40 M.A. 2417 by driving it rashly and negligently dashed the appellant, due to which she suffered fracture in right leg and other injuries on different parts of her body.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal has erroneously dismissed the claim petition on the ground that factum of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14177 2 MA-745-2009 accident is not proved.
The learned Tribunal has wrongly stated in para 6 of the impugned award that registration number of the offending vehicle was not intimated to the claimant by other ladies accompanying her.

It is also submitted while drawing attention of this Court towards the statement of appellant/claimant Guddi Bai (AW-1) that she in para 7 has categorically stated that she did not know Rakesh Sharma, the driver of the offending vehicle, but other ladies accompanying her, intimated the name of driver of the offending vehicle.
Keeping in view the entire statement of claimant Guddi Bai (AW-1) as well as the documents Ex.P/1 to Ex.P/5, the factum of accident is proved.

It is also submitted that learned Tribunal has erroneously not found proved that any permanent disability has been caused to the claimant, while as per the statement of Dr. P.L.Arya (AW-2) the claimant has sustained 25% permanent disability in her right leg.
Tibia and fibula bone of right leg was fractured and and there was dis-figuration.
It is also submitted that learned Tribunal has not considered the evidence of income of the claimant.

As per the minimum wages declared by the Labour Department, the minimum wages of an unskilled labourer on the date of accident was Smt.Guddi Bai vs Rakesh Sharma on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109245134/
1 Rs.2,584/-, therefore, the learned Tribunal ought to have assumed it as the income of the appellant and assessed the compensation accordingly.

entities.text: Smt.Guddi Bai vs Rakesh Sharma on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant has also submitted bills and cash memos for purchasing medicines etc. during treatment which may also be taken into consideration.

Hence,
prayed for setting aside the impugned award and awarding compensation amount accordingly.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14177 3 MA-745-2009 opposed the prayer on the ground that learned Tribunal has rightly found on the basis of evidence on record that factum of accident is not proved,
therefore, other assessment was not necessary by learned Tribunal.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.
6.
Guddi Bai (AW-1) herself is an eye-witness to the accident because she sustained injury in the accident.

She categorically stated in her chief- examination that when she was going with other ladies for labour work on 16.09.2007 at 11 am suddenly the offending vehicle Ishar tractor bearing registration No.MP40/MA 2417 being driven by its driver rashly and negligently hit her right leg,
therefore, she sustained fracture in right leg and also sustained injury on other parts of the body.
She remained admitted in Hamidiya Hospital, Bhopal and thereafter she got treatment from hospital at Vidisha.
She has submitted papers regarding the offence registered by the police as Ex.P/1 to Ex.P/5.
Ex . P/2
is the FIR which has been registered on the information received by police.
Ex .P/2
reveals registration number of the offending vehicle in para 9 and on that information police Karariya Distt.
Vidisha has registered an offence under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC against driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereafter the offending vehicle has been seized vide Ex.P/3.
MLC and X-ray report of injured Guddi Bai is Ex.P/4 and Ex.P/5.

After completion of investigation, the police submitted a Challan (Ex.P/1) before the concerning Court against driver of the offending vehicle/respondent No.1- Rakesh Sharma under Sections 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14177 4 MA-745-2009 7.

Though it is revealed from the cross-examination of Guddi Bai (AW-1) that she has not seen registration number of the tractor and she has not informed the police about registration number of the tractor, but she stated that the tractor was being driven by Rakesh Sharma.
Though she did not know Rakesh Sharma earlier, but the name of the driver was asked by the ladies accompanying her.
No other fact reveals from the cross-examination of this witness to disbelieve her testimony.
The learned Tribunal has erred in concluding that the accident is not found proved as stated in the claim petition.
Argument of learned counsel for the appellant in that respect is found to be acceptable.
There is no rebuttal evidence on behalf of non- applicants.

8.. In the case of Bimla Devi vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation AIR 2009 SC 2819 it is ruled by the Hon'ble Apex Court that in claim cases the claimant is not under the obligation to adduce cogent evidence.

entities.text: Bimla Devi vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation AIR 2009 SC 2819
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claim cases are to be decided on the principle of preponderance of probability.
Principle of beyond reasonable doubt is not applicable in such cases.

Smt. Guddi Bai vs Rakesh Sharma on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109245134/
2 9.

In the case of Rajendra Singh vs. Sheetal Das, 1992(1) M.P.W.N. 104 , it has been observed that if the driver of the offending vehicle is not examined on behalf of the non-applicants, a presumption may be drawn against him that he was driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligently.

entities.text: Rajendra Singh vs. Sheetal Das, 1992(1) M.P.W.N. 104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In the case of National Insurance Company Ltd vs. Sanjay Kumar & Ors., II(2011) ACC 75 it has been held by the Punjab & Haryana High Court that when driver of the offending vehicle is facing criminal trial, prima facie it can be presumed that he was responsible for accident.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd vs. Sanjay Kumar & Ors., II(2011) ACC 75
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14177 5 MA-745-2009 11.

Having considered the law laid down in aforesaid cases, since there is no rebuttal evidence on record against the evidence of claimant and the driver of the offending vehicle has not examined himself before learned Tribunal as well as that evidence of claimant is found to be believable supported by documentary evidence, therefore, the factum of accident as stated in the claim petition is found to be proved.
Being erroneous, the conclusion of learned Tribunal on issue No.1 is liable to be set aside.

12. As regards permanent disability to the claimant is concerned, Dr. P.L.Arya (AW-2) has though stated that he has issued permanent disability certificate in favour of the claimant as Ex.P/23 which is showing 25% permanent disability to the claimant, but he admitted in his cross- examination that he has not treated the claimant nor prepared pre-MLC.
Both the bones of right leg have been conveniently joined.
He also categorically admitted in his cross-examination that he has not given any basis for calculating the percentage of permanent disability in Ex.P/23.
He has found deformity in the leg of appellant/claimant.

The learned Tribunal has found this statement and Ex.P/23 insufficient for establishing the fact of permanent disability on the basis of provisions of Section 142 of the Motor Vehicles Act which being relevant is reproduced as infra:-
"142. Permanent disablement . For the purposes of this chapter, permanent disablement of a person shall be deemed to have resulted from an accident of the nature referred to in sub-section (1) of Sec. 140 if such person has suffered by reason of the accident, any injury or injuries involving:
(a) permanent privation of the sight of either eye or the hearing of either ear, or privation of any member or joint; or (b) destruction or permanent impairing of the powers of any member or joint; or (c) permanent disfiguration of the head or face."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14177 6 MA-745-2009 13.

The perusal of the statement of Dr. P.L.Arya (AW-2) shows that on the ground of finding deformity in the right leg of the claimant, he has issued disability certificate (Ex.P/23), but no ground for assumption of such permanent disability has either been stated in Ex.P/23 or in the Smt.Guddi Bai vs Rakesh Sharma on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109245134/
3 statement by this witness (AW-2).
Therefore, only on the basis of deformity in the right leg, it cannot be held that the claimant has sustained permanent disability.

To establish the fact of permanent disability, it ought to be established by the claimant that there was movement restriction in right leg or right leg was shortened or any other disability has been caused in right leg.
The burden of proving permanent disability which was on the claimant has not been satisfactorily discharged by her as per the provisions of Section 142 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Hence, the conclusion of learned Tribunal on issue No.2 is not found to be faulted with or perverse, and as such, is affirmed.
1 4 . The conclusion of learned Tribunal on issue No.3 has not been challenged by the claimant.

The learned Tribunal has not assessed the amount of compensation, but for this purpose only, remand of the matter to the learned Tribunal, does not seem to be appropriate in the interest of justice because the accident occurred in 2007 and this appeal is pending in this Court since 2009

, therefore,
calculation of amount of compensation can very well be done by this Court in this appeal.
15. Claimant/appellant has stated in her statement that she was doing labour work.

On the date of accident, the minimum wages of an unskilled NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14177 7 MA-745-2009 labourer were Rs.2,584/- per month which can appropriately be considered as the income of the claimant.
She sustained grievous injury in her right leg, therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, six months' income ought to be granted in favour of claimant.
The claimant has submitted total bills of purchasing medicines of Rs.7,077/-.
The claimant must have also incurred expenses towards special diet, attender expenses and transportation charges etc.
On these heads, in the considered opinion of this Court, the claimant is entitled to get Rs.40,000/-.

Keeping in view the nature of grievous injury caused to the claimant, in the considered opinion of this Court,
the claimant is entitled to Rs.50,000/- on the head of pain & suffering.

16. Consequently, the appeal is allowed in above terms and the appellant would be entitled for the following compensation:-
Amount of Compensation Sr.No. Head assessed by this Court Loss of income during treatment (6 1. 15,504/-
months) Medical expenses, Special diet, attender 2. 40,000/-
expenses and transportation charges 3.

Pain & suffering 50,000/-
4.
This amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of the claim application.
